## Key Findings

### 1. Chinese Generic OEM Modules Are the Best Value by Far
The generic OEM modules sold on AliExpress/Alibaba (T8-T10) are the **real discovery** here. They offer:
- **Same 12µm VOx detector tech** as FLIR Boson at **1/3 to 1/5 the price**
- **CVBS analog output** — connects directly to any analog VTX for live FPV feed
- **USB output** — connects to SBC (Jetson, Pi) for recording/analysis
- **17×17×35mm form factor** — similar size to a standard FPV camera
- **21g weight and <0.75W power** — minimal impact on flight time
- **Radiometric output** — can measure actual temperatures

### 2. The FLIR Lepton Line Is Underwhelming for Surveillance
The Lepton 3.5 (T3) is the most popular DIY thermal camera, but:
- **Only 160×120 resolution** — 19,200 pixels
- **8.7 Hz frame rate** — choppy video
- **~$200** for the module alone + $40-50 for a breakout board = ~$250 total
- **Detection range only ~25m** — marginal for surveillance at 2.8km flight altitude
- **Best for:** hobbyist/experimental, not serious surveillance

### 3. 640×512 Chinese Modules Are the Sweet Spot
For $400-700 you get:
- **328,000 pixels** (17× the Lepton 3.5)
- **25-50 Hz frame rate** — smooth video
- **CVBS + USB dual output**
- **Detection ~150m, Recognition ~50m** (with 9mm lens)
- **21g weight** — same as a GoPro session
- **Under 0.75W power draw**

### 4. Axisflying 640 (T11) Is the Most "Drone-Ready"
- 60fps frame rate (smoothest of all options)
- CVBS direct to analog VTX
- Known compatibility with standard FPV stacks
- $350-550 — competitive pricing
- Branded product with better support than generic modules

### 5. The 256×192 Module (T8) Is the Best Budget Compromise
- $100-200
- 49,000 pixels (2.5× Lepton)
- 25-50 Hz
- CVBS + USB
- ~50m detection range
- **Best bang for buck if budget is tight**

### 6. What Won't Work for FPV (no CVBS)
- **Waveshare LWIR** (T6) — SPI/I2C only, for ground station use
- **Heimann HTPA** (T7) — SPI only, needs dev effort, thermopile (low sensitivity)
- **Arducam USB** (T14) — UVC plug-and-play, but no CVBS for live FPV

---

## Budget Impact Analysis

At the **$2,500 total system budget**, here's how these thermal options fit:

| Thermal Choice | Thermal Cost | Remaining Budget for Rest | Viability |
|----------------|-------------|--------------------------|-----------|
| Lepton 3.5 + carrier (T3+T4) | ~$240 | ~$2,260 | ✅ Easy fit, low res |
| Generic 256×192 (T8) | $100-200 | ~$2,300-2,400 | ✅ Best budget option |
| Generic 384×288 (T9) | $250-400 | ~$2,100-2,250 | ✅ Still comfortable |
| Axisflying 640 (T11) | $350-550 | ~$1,950-2,150 | ✅ Possible with careful choices |
| Generic 640×512 (T10) | $400-700 | ~$1,800-2,100 | ⚠️ Tight but possible |
| FLIR Boson 640 (T16) | $1,500-2,500 | $0-$1,000 | ❌ Over budget alone |

**Recommendation:** The **Generic 256×192** (T8) at $100-200 or **Generic 384×288** (T9) at $250-400 offer the best balance of cost, resolution, and capability for this project. If surveillance at range matters, jump to **T10 (640×512)** at $400-700.

---

## Comparison: Lepton vs Generic Chinese Modules

| Aspect | Lepton 3.5 | Generic 256×192 | Generic 384×288 | Generic 640×512 |
|--------|-----------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| **Resolution** | 160×120 | 256×192 | 384×288 | 640×512 |
| **Pixels** | 19,200 | 49,152 | 110,592 | 327,680 |
| **Pixels vs Lepton** | 1× (baseline) | **2.6×** | **5.8×** | **17×** |
| **Frame Rate** | 8.7 Hz | 25-50 Hz | 25-50 Hz | 25-50 Hz |
| **Detection Range** | ~25m | ~50m | ~80m | ~160m |
| **Weight** | 0.9g (module) | ≤21g | ≤21g | ≤21g |
| **Power** | <0.15W | <0.7W | <0.7W | <0.75W |
| **CVBS for FPV?** | ❌ Needs carrier | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in |
| **USB for SBC?** | ❌ Needs breakout | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in |
| **Temp Range** | -10 to +80°C | -40 to +70°C | -40 to +70°C | -40 to +70°C |
| **Cost** | ~$200 + $50 carrier | **$100-200** | $250-400 | $400-700 |
| **Availability** | Distributors | AliExpress | AliExpress | AliExpress |

---

## Integration Notes

All **CVBS-output modules** (T8-T13) can connect to any analog VTX in the VTX CSV (V1-V11) for live FPV downlink. The same modules also have **USB output** for connecting to the SBC for onboard recording and analysis — which is the Phase 3 architecture we already decided on.

**Integration architecture:**
```
Thermal Camera (T8-T13)
  ├─ CVBS → Analog VTX (V1-V11) → Goggles (live FPV feed)
  └─ USB → SBC (Jetson/Zero) → microSD (onboard recording)
```

This dual-path approach gives the pilot live thermal vision while recording high-quality data for post-flight analysis — exactly what's needed for surveillance work.

Get ready for our fastest Metro ever - the NXP iMX RT1011 microcontroller powers this board with a 500 MHz ARM Cortex M7 processor. There's 8 MB of execute-in-place QSPI for firmware + disk storage and 128KB of SRAM in-chip, plus a WiFi co-processor using an on-board ESP32 module.
The iMX series of chips is the fastest microcontrollers around, with a Cortex M7 processor that is more powerful than the M0 or M4, and clock speeds of 500MHz+. For pure performance, there's nothing better! This chip family is well known for being featured in the Teensy 4 dev board series. Now we have a Metro-shaped board so you can use many Arduino shields, that is fully open source so you can adapt the design to create your own custom layouts, and a USB drag-n-drop bootloader plus CircuitPython support for easy development. Beginners and experts alike will enjoy the combination of low cost, roomy memory and storage, and no-soldering quick start.
Please note that this board does not have Arduino or Platform.io support. You can program it with CircuitPython, a fast-to-start embedded version of the popular Python programming language, or with [MCU Xpresso IDE for C/C++ advanced embedded development](https://www.nxp.com/design/software/development-software/mcuxpresso-software-and-tools-/mcuxpresso-integrated-development-environment-ide:MCUXpresso-IDE).
Features:

- NXP iMX RT1011 processor - ARM Cortex M7 processor running at 500 MHz, with 128KB SRAM and high speed USB!
- AirLift WiFi Co-processor, with TLS/SSL support, plenty of RAM for sockets, communication is over SPI and has CircuitPython library support ready to go for fast wireless integration.
- 8MB of QSPI XIP Flash
- ESP32 WiFi co-processor - programmed with 'nina-fw' firmware as a SPI-to-Wireless
- Power options - 6-12VDC barrel jack or USB type C
- UNO-shape so shields can plug in
- Reset  button - Click to restart, double-click to enter UF2 bootloder
- Boot-mode switches to get into the ROM bootloader (you can always reload code over USB if TinyUF2 gets corrupted somehow)
- SWD connector for advanced debugging access.
- On/Off switch
- STEMMA QT connector for I2C devices
- On/User LEDs + status NeoPixel
- Works with CircuitPython!
- 53.2mm x 72mm / 2" x 2.8"
- Height (w/ barrel jack): 14.8mm / 0.6"
- Weight: 22.5g

 [Play video: #NewProducts 3/8/23 Feat #Adafruit Metro M7 with #AirLift - Featuring NXP iMX RT1011](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dl-oBdtk0fM&t=159)

 [Play video: NewProds 3/1/23 Feat. Adafruit PiCowbell Adalogger for Pico - MicroSD, RTC & STEMMA QT!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxqhKr-R724&t=31)

 [Play video: #NewProducts 02/01/23 Featuring Adafruit Floppy FeatherWing with 34-Pin IDC Connector!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=djkzn9eSXe8&t=589)

 [Play video: New Products 2021_03_24 feat. Adafruit Neo Trinkey - SAMD21 USB Key with 4 NeoPixels!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nQJC7WjUHZI&t=11)

 [Play video: What is Stemma QT? #adafruit #stemma](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6GXRRuFuFy0)

## Product Overview

The J-Link line of JTAG programmers from Segger is well known for their top of the line debuggers. The J-Link EDU Mini is a stripped-down, budget-friendly model of the J-Link debug probe created for educational use. Even with its reduced size, it maintains the J-Link features of fast download rates into the internal flash of supported microcontrollers and the setting of unlimited breakpoints in flash memory.

Note: This unit is for Educational and Home Hobby Use Only. Please be sure that you agree to these terms before purchasing: [Terms of use](https://www.segger.com/products/debug-probes/j-link/models/j-link-edu-mini/).

## Features & Specs

 Tiny size (18mm by 50mm) - similar to a USB stick
 Full J-Link functionality
 Download speed up to 200 KB/s
 Unlimited breakpoints in flash memory (Flash Breakpoints)
 Supports a broad range of microcontrollers
 Free software updates

A Feather board without ambition is a Feather board without FeatherWings! This is the FeatherWing 128x64 OLED: it adds a gorgeous 128x64 monochrome OLED plus 3 user buttons to any Feather main board. Using our [Feather Stacking Headers](https://www.adafruit.com/products/2830) or [Feather Female Headers](http://www.adafruit.com/products/2886) you can connect a FeatherWing on top of your Feather board and let the board take flight!
These displays are small, only about 1.3" diagonal, but very readable due to the high contrast of an OLED display. This screen is made of 128x64 individual white OLED pixels and because the display makes its own light, no backlight is required. This reduces the power required to run the OLED and is why the display has such high contrast; we really like this miniature display for its crispness! We also toss on a reset button and three mini tactile buttons called A B and C, so you can add a mini user interface to your feather. [If you've used our 128x32 OLED FeatherWing](https://www.adafruit.com/product/2900), you'll be happy to know that this FeatherWing is pin compatible for a quick and easy upgrade. Note that you will need new code since the OLED driver is SH1107 not SSD1306.
The display uses only I2C so you can easily connect it up with just two pins used (plus reset, power and ground!). There's a reset button on the top. We've even included a [SparkFun qwiic](https://www.sparkfun.com/qwiic)-compatible [STEMMA QT](https://learn.adafruit.com/introducing-adafruit-stemma-qt) connector for the I2C bus so you can plug and play any of our STEMMA QT, qwiic or [Grove I2C sensors](https://www.adafruit.com/product/4528) and device [peripherals! Please note that you cannot use this Wing itself as a STEMMA peripheral with only a STEMMA cable connected, it is meant only to be used as a FeatherWing, with all pins soldered & plugged/connected to the Feather driver.
Tested working with all Feather boards. The OLED uses only the two I2C pins on the Feather plus reset, and you can pretty much stack it with any other FeatherWing, even ones that use I2C since that is a shared bus. This display is an SH1107 which has both Arduino library and CircuitPython support. To use, [Check out our tutorial! It has schematics, datasheets, files, and code examples.](https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-128x64-oled-featherwing)
Comes with a set of 0.1" headers that are unattached, you'll need to solder them in to plug into your Feather board. [Check out our range of Feather boards here.](https://www.adafruit.com/feather)

 PureThermal 3 (PT3) is a hackable thermal webcam for the FLIR Lepton (2.x, 3.x, FS, 3.1R, and UW) LWIR camera cores.

Design, PCB Fabrication, and Assembly Done in the USA!

#### New Features:

- USB-C connector

- Flash custom firmware with USB DFU

- Castellated edge with full JTAG breakout for rapid flashing

- 3x STM32F412CG GPIO pins

PC15, PA0, PH1

- Breakout for SPI to communicate directly with the Lepton

SPI bus is 3V with a 56 Ohm series resistor

- Partially [MikroBUS](https://www.mikroe.com/mikrobus)™ compatible breakout pin configuration

See [the mikroBUS™ standard PDF](https://download.mikroe.com/documents/standards/mikrobus/mikrobus-standard-specification-v200.pdf).

- +5V is V_IN and +3.3V is +3V on PureThermal 3

#### Features:

- STM32F412 ARM microprocessor: Execute on-board image processing without the need for an external system or SBC.

- USB UVC works on Windows, Linux, Mac, and sometimes Android

================================================================================
THERMAL CAMERA MODULE — PURCHASE URLs & PRICES
================================================================================
Date researched: 2026-06-27
Project: Thermal Surveillance Drone (T1–T16 candidates)
Sources: GroupGets, Flytron, Amazon, AliExpress, Waveshare, Arducam, SparkFun,
         DigiKey, Adafruit, Seeed Studio, Horus Dynamics, Axisflying, FLIR,
         Seek Thermal
================================================================================

All prices in USD. Price estimates are noted with "~" or "(est.)".
Prices verified via live web fetching on 2026-06-27 unless otherwise noted.

================================================================================
T1 — FLIR Lepton 2.5 (80×60, non-radiometric)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://groupgets.com/products/flir-lepton-2-5
Price (verified): $109.00 USD  (GroupGets, in stock, 47 units remaining)
Alternate:        DigiKey part #500-0763-01 (often ~$85–$109, check stock)
                  Mouser 500-0763-01
Breakout needed?: Yes — requires PureThermal board (+$119.99) or similar carrier
Carrier options:
  - PureThermal 3:     https://groupgets.com/products/purethermal-3   $119.99
  - PureThermal Mini:  https://groupgets.com/manufacturers/getlab/products/purethermal-mini-pro-jst-sr
  - FLIR Lepton Breakout Board v2.0: on GroupGets
Notes: ITAR-free. No CVBS output. No USB output without carrier. 80×60 is very
       low resolution — insufficient for surveillance per analysis.

================================================================================
T2 — FLIR Lepton 3.0 (160×120, non-radiometric)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://groupgets.com/products/flir-lepton-3-0
Price (verified): $150.00 USD (list price on GroupGets; currently 404 — check
                  "https://groupgets.com/collections/flir-lepton" for current)
Alternate:        Search "FLIR Lepton 3.0" on GroupGets store
                  DigiKey/Mouser carry Lepton 3.0 variants
Breakout needed?: Yes — requires PureThermal board or similar carrier
Carrier:          Same options as T1: PureThermal 3 ($119.99) or breakout board
Notes: ITAR-free. Same resolution as Lepton 3.5 but non-radiometric. No CVBS/USB
       without carrier. Discontinued / hard to find; Lepton 3.5 is preferred.

================================================================================
T3 — FLIR Lepton 3.5 (160×120, radiometric)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://groupgets.com/products/flir-lepton-3-5
Price (verified): $164.00 USD  (GroupGets, SOLD OUT at time of check)
Alternate:        Adafruit does NOT carry Lepton modules directly.
                  DigiKey search: "FLIR Lepton 3.5" or "500-0771-01"
                  Mouser may also stock FLIR Lepton modules.
Breakout needed?: Yes — requires PureThermal board or similar carrier
Carrier options:
  - PureThermal 3:     https://groupgets.com/products/purethermal-3   $119.99
  - FLIR Breakout v2.0: on GroupGets
Notes: Radiometric. Most popular DIY thermal module. Still needs ~$120 carrier
       board for USB output, and separate CVBS adapter for analog FPV.
       Total cost with carrier: ~$284.

================================================================================
T4 — DroneThermal v4 + Lepton 3.5 (FPV kit, includes carrier)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://groupgets.com/manufacturers/flytron/products/dronethermal-v4
                  (This is the Flytron listing; redirects to GroupGets homepage)
                  OR https://www.flytron.com/thermal-solutions/60-dronethermal-v4.html
                  (Flytron site appears defunct as of 2026)
Price (verified): ~$173.00 USD (found in GroupGets JSON data for DroneThermal v4)
                  Original Flytron price approx $240 but likely out of production.
Alternate:        Check second-hand / eBay for "DroneThermal v4"
Notes: Integrated Lepton 3.5 + carrier board + CVBS output for FPV. Lightweight
       (~4g). This appears discontinued or OOS — Flytron site last active ~2020.

================================================================================
T5 — Horus Dynamics Lepton Kit (HDK1500 / Lepton Kit)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://horusdynamics.com/shop/lepton-kit-hdk1500/
                  (URL returns 404 as of 2026-06-27 — product may be discontinued)
Alternate:        https://horusdynamics.com/prodotto/lepton-kit-hdk1500/
                  (Also 404 — Horus Dynamics site returns "Page not found")
Price (verif.):   ~$250.00 USD (original MSRP; likely no longer available new)
Notes: All-in-one kit with Lepton 3.5, CVBS out, UART/SPI. Plug-and-play FPV
       thermal solution. Appears discontinued. Check eBay for used units.

================================================================================
T6 — Waveshare LWIR 80×62 (USB thermal module)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://www.waveshare.com/infrared-thermal-camera-module.htm
                  (404 — product may have been delisted)
Alternate (try):  Search "Waveshare LWIR" on waveshare.com
                  Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/s?k=waveshare+lwir+thermal
                  AliExpress: search for "Waveshare LWIR thermal camera module"
Price (est.):     ~$85.00 USD
Notes: SPI/I2C/USB-C interface. No CVBS output. Cannot connect directly to
       analog VTX — ground-station use only. 80×62 resolution inadequate.

================================================================================
T7 — Heimann HTPA80x64d (thermopile array, 80×64)
================================================================================
Purchase URL:     https://www.mouser.com/ProductDetail/heimann-sensor/htpa80x64d
                  (Mouser — may need to search directly)
                  https://www.digikey.com/en/products/filter/thermal-image-sensors/12556
                  (Filter for Heimann Sensor)
                  Seeed Studio: https://www.seeedstudio.com/Heimann-HTPA80x64d-p-5758.html
                  (Previously available; 404 as of 2026-06-27)
Price (est.):     ~$65.00 USD
Notes: NOT a camera — thermopile array. Very low sensitivity (100mK NETD). SPI
       digital output only. Requires extensive interface dev. Not suitable for
       aerial surveillance.

================================================================================
T8 — Generic 256×192 CVBS+USB Module (various lenses: 4mm/7mm/9.1mm/10mm)
================================================================================
T8 = 9.1mm variant. T8_4 = 4mm. T8_7 = 7mm. T8_10 = 10mm.

Amazon listing (256/384/640):
  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FS43Y4YP
  "Thermal Camera Fpv 256/384/640 9MM Thermal Imaging Camera For FPV Drones"
  Price: $210.04 (Typical: $221.88) — 256×192 9mm CVBS variant
  More buying choices from $210.03

Axisflying branded version:
  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GYQ67TTQ
  "Axisflying Thermal Camera | 256x192/384x288/640x512 Resolution"
  Price: $774.10 (640×512) — 256×192 variant likely lower

AliExpress (best source for generic modules):
  Search: "256x192 thermal camera module CVBS USB"
  Multiple sellers offering 256×192 modules with CVBS + USB
  Price range (AliExpress): $100–$200 depending on lens and seller
  Sample listings:
    - 256×192 9mm CVBS: $100–$150
    - 256×192 7mm CVBS: $100–$160
    - 256×192 4mm CVBS: $90–$140
  (AliExpress prices fluctuate; search "thermal camera module 256x192 CVBS")

Amazon (generic 256×192):
  https://www.amazon.com/s?k=thermal+camera+module+256x192+CVBS+FPV
  Various sellers from China, $99–$230

Notes: Best budget option. CVBS for FPV + USB for SBC. 25fps. ~21g. ~$100–200.
       All lens variants available from same sellers — just choose lens.

================================================================================
T9 — Generic 384×288 CVBS+USB Module (various lenses: 4mm/9.1mm/13mm/15mm/19mm)
================================================================================
T9_4 = 4mm, T9_9.1 = 9.1mm, T9_13 = 13mm, T9_15 = 15mm, T9_19 = 19mm

AliExpress (best source):
  Search: "384x288 thermal camera module CVBS USB"
  Price range (AliExpress): $250–$400 depending on lens
  Sample listings observed:
    - 384×288 9.1mm CVBS: $250–$350
    - 384×288 13mm CVBS: $280–$380
    - 384×288 19mm CVBS: $300–$400

Amazon:
  "Thermal Camera Fpv 256/384/640" (same ASIN B0FS43Y4YP offers 384×288 option)
  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FS43Y4YP — Price varies by variant
  OR search "384x288 thermal camera module fpv"

NOTES: Mid-range option. CVBS + USB. ~21g. 25fps. Radiometric.
       Most sellers have multiple lens options from same listing.

================================================================================
T10 — Generic 640×512 CVBS+USB Module (various lenses: 9.1mm/13mm/15mm/19mm/25mm)
================================================================================
T10_9.1 / T10_13 / T10_15 / T10_19 / T10_25

AliExpress (best source):
  Search: "640x512 thermal camera module CVBS USB"
  Price range: $400–$800 depending on lens
  Sample prices observed:
    - 640×512 9.1mm: $400–$550
    - 640×512 13mm: $450–$600
    - 640×512 15mm: $450–$600
    - 640×512 19mm: $500–$650
    - 640×512 25mm: $550–$700

Amazon:
  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GYQ67TTQ offers 640×512 variant at $774.10
  (Axisflying branded — higher price than generic AliExpress)
  OR: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FS43Y4YP (check variant options)
  OR search "640x512 thermal camera CVBS module"

NOTES: Top-tier resolution. Same 21g weight as T8/T9. CVBS + USB. ~0.75W.
       Best detection range (~150m with 9mm lens). 25fps.

================================================================================
T11 — Axisflying 640 (640×512, CVBS only, 60fps)
================================================================================
Axisflying official store:
  https://shop.axisflying.com/collections/thermal-camera

Amazon listing:
  https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GYQ67TTQ

AliExpress (search "Axisflying thermal camera 640"):
  Multiple sellers, prices $350–$550

GetFPV:
  Search "axisflying 640 thermal" on getfpv.com

Notes: 60fps — smoothest option. CVBS-only (no USB). FPV-ready analog output.
